projects.title: Somalia Crisis Recovery Project MIS: Power BI upgrade and handover
projects.clientFull: United Nations Office for Project Services (UNOPS)
projects.challenge: The World Bank-funded Somalia Crisis Recovery Project already had a Power BI MIS, but it needed maintenance and targeted upgrades. Grievance data was buried inside the environmental and social section where it was hard to read, and free-text data entry had left the records full of inconsistent spellings and spacing.
projects.whatWeDid: Over two months, from March to May 2026, we enhanced six Power BI modules. We turned grievance redress into its own three-page module with gender breakdowns and rebuilt environmental and social safeguards as a seven-page module with site compliance, photo evidence and a register. We set up Google Sheets trackers with dropdowns and protected headers, trained the PIU team and handed the system over.

results.label: Technical handover to the PIU confirmed on 17 May 2026

projects.title: Disaster Risk Reduction and Early Warning training video series
projects.credit: Produced with Magan Graphics and Media
services: 4K masters with web and mobile versions
projects.challenge: Community leaders, government officers and NGO workers in Southwest State face recurring floods, droughts and displacement. Early warning data from systems like SWALIM, FSNAU and Saadaal exists, but the people who need to act on it often lack practical, accessible training in their own language.
projects.whatWeDid: We are producing a five-part bilingual training series of about 10 minutes per video, covering resilience foundations, early warning tools and how to read them, last-mile warning communication, community preparedness and institutional coordination. Presenter segments filmed in a Mogadishu studio are combined with field footage, drone shots and animated explainers from across the region. We also delivered a two-presenter course promo, a 108-asset shot list and register, and an inception report.

projects.title: TIGAAL institutional website and admin portal
projects.challenge: TIGAAL needed an authoritative digital presence to position itself as a social enterprise and consulting firm in the Horn of Africa, plus an in-house system to manage proposals, field projects, team profiles and publications without depending on outside help.
projects.whatWeDid: We built and deployed an institutional website with dedicated pages for nine core capabilities, filterable projects and an evaluation report library. Behind it, we built a custom admin portal with a business development pipeline in Kanban and list views, content management for team and projects, and automatic handling of contact enquiries.

projects.title: Closure workshops and asset handover for two Galmudug sites
projects.clientFull: United Nations Office for Project Services (UNOPS) Somalia
projects.challenge: Two World Bank-funded Somalia Crisis Recovery Project sites in Galmudug had to be formally closed out and handed to state authorities. That meant gathering and recording stakeholder feedback, and making sure local staff could run and maintain the assets.
projects.whatWeDid: We facilitated two stakeholder engagement and handover workshops, in Dhusamareb on 16 May 2026 and Adado on 19 May 2026, and delivered operations, maintenance and training at Adado General Hospital. We wrote the field mission memo and a final report that answered a 42-comment review, with 16 captioned field photographs and copy for LinkedIn and the web.

results.label: Formal handover records signed, transferring the assets to Galmudug State authorities
Stakeholders took part across the two workshops
Of Adado participants were women (28 of 40)

projects.title: Somalia Crisis Recovery Project: communication and visibility across three states
projects.clientFull: United Nations Office for Project Services (UNOPS)
projects.location: Hirshabelle, Jubbaland and South West States, Somalia
projects.challenge: The World Bank-financed Somalia Crisis Recovery Project had finished building health centres, hospital units, roads, drainage canals and a river embankment across three federal member states, but it had no visual record or stories to show what those projects achieved.
projects.whatWeDid: We filmed and photographed finished project sites across Hirshabelle, Jubbaland and South West States, collecting interviews with beneficiaries and officials, drone footage and coverage of community workshops. In a post-production hub in Mogadishu we edited five video stories, against a contract minimum of three. We also wrote five success stories, each backed by a signed consent form, and produced a set of infographics.

projects.title: Strategic communications plan for peacebuilding
projects.clientFull: Life and Peace Institute (LPI), with Somali Public Agenda (SPA)
projects.location: Mogadishu and Federal Member States, Somalia
services: CSO communication and social media training
projects.challenge: LPI and SPA were running an EU-funded peacebuilding and reconciliation programme across several Federal Member States without a shared communications approach. Peace messaging in Somalia is conflict-sensitive by nature: content that lands badly in one community can set back work across all of them.
projects.whatWeDid: We designed and facilitated participatory workshops with LPI, SPA and civil society partners across the Federal Member States and Mogadishu, then built a strategic communications plan aligned to LPI's 2023 to 2028 Strategic Plan. We developed peace messaging frameworks and content validation tools to keep output conflict-sensitive and inclusive, and trained CSO networks on communication, social media and peace narratives.

projects.title: Maan Hotel website, booking system and QR cafe menu
projects.challenge: Maan Hotel needed a website to show its rooms and cafe and take booking enquiries. Staff also needed a simple way to manage bookings, photos and the cafe menu without a developer.
projects.whatWeDid: We built a multi-page website with rooms, cafe, gallery, location and contact pages, and booking forms that save each enquiry and open WhatsApp with the guest's details filled in. Staff run it from an admin panel with orders, users, gallery uploads and a menu of 14 categories and 101 items. Guests scan QR codes at tables and in rooms to open a mobile menu with food photos.

projects.title: SOWDA website and content management system
projects.challenge: SOWDA's content was stored directly in the website's code, so routine updates needed a developer. The site also lacked separate page addresses and a secure way to manage content.
projects.whatWeDid: We redesigned the website with dedicated pages for the organisation, programs, projects, news, involvement, donations, contact, privacy and careers. We connected programs, projects, thematic areas, initiatives, news and resources to a database, and built a secure admin panel with publishing controls, rich text editing and image uploads.

projects.title: Danab: one workspace for projects, planning, clients and invoices
projects.challenge: Independent operators were stretched across many apps to manage projects, plan work, track clients and prepare invoices. Danab brings those jobs into one workspace.
projects.whatWeDid: We designed and built Danab with project tracking, daily tasks, a weekly planner with separate weekly priorities, a Pomodoro timer, client management, invoices and quotations, plus account access and user administration.
